newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS - Mexico's Comerci goes it alone.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mexico's Comerci goes it alone.

text.p: Mexico's Controlador Comercial Mexicana SA (Comerci) has decided to go it alone in the local retail market at a time when its rivals have hitched their fortunes to foreign partners.

Mexico's second-biggest retailer said on Friday it had broken off its joint venture with Groupe Auchan, France's fourth-largest retailer, whose business is focused on building large-scale stores known as hypermarkets.
At the same time, Comerci said it would pay $149 million to buy Kmart de Mexico SA, a joint venture between U.S.-based Kmart Corp and local retailer El Puerto de Liverpool SA.
The deal will increase Comerci's floor sales space by 7.2 percent, adding four Kmart hypermarkets in Mexico City and elsewhere and one Kmart store due to open soon in the central city of Puebla.
Also, Comerci will keep one existing hypermarket from its operation with Auchan and allow the French retailer to keep two others slated to open in the coming months.
Industry analysts said Comerci may have dumped Auchan because the French retailer planned a more aggressive initial expansion that would have extended the pay-back period.

Still, analysts were surprised at the decision, with so many other Mexican retailers teaming up with foreign partners. Market leader Cifra SA is believed to be negotiating with U.S.-based Wal-Mart about deepening their relationship in the coming months.
Comerci's partnership with Auchan has helped improve the Mexican retailer's efficiency, and some analysts were concerned it could have ended the arrangement too soon.

"Instead of having an experienced partner to help follow through with efficiency improvements, Comerci now has a strong, possibly more aggressive, competitor (in Auchan)," said Marc de Speville, an analyst at Robert Flemings.
In addition, some analysts said they feared Comerci may have overpaid for the Kmart stores, with the U.S. retailer thought to be eager to sell assets. Comerci may have been the only bidder.
Perhaps more troubling for some, the move will raise the retailer's debt from $165 million to $285 million only months after the company issued equity to draw down its high dollar debt.
"They just got out of their debt problem with the equity offering and now they are going to take on more debt," said Shannon O'Neil, an analyst at Credit Lyonnais in New York.
Comerci has a Eurobond worth $110 million that comes due in 1998, making the company vulnerable to potential losses by the peso, which could increase its dollar debt, analysts said.
Investors were clearly worried on Friday, driving down Comerci's UB shares on the Mexican Bolsa by 7.51 percent.
Smith Barney brokerage lowered its rating on Comerci to market underperform from neutral because of concern about the deal.

According to analysts, company officials on Friday said in a conference call they would need to finance about $120 million of the Kmart transaction by obtaining a bridge loan and later issuing longer-term debt on the international markets.
